style: Say in a relaxed, friendly way, like a kind dad helping with homework
lines: This is Star Catch. Each box under the game is a variable, and it holds one value. Press Play to start, and steer with the arrow buttons or the arrow keys.
You caught a star, so the score line ran. Score got bigger by the star's points, and the old value is gone.
Ouch, a rock. The lives line ran and took the rock's amount from lives.
Ten seconds went by, so speed went up. Nobody pressed anything. Time changed that one.
Lives got to zero or less, so the game ended.
Score reached the goal, so the game ended.
Score was more than best, so best saved it.
Game over. Press Play again and watch which boxes start over.
Press Save to notebook to keep this run. Then press Run again, or turn a dial first.
New game. Score, lives and speed went back to their starting values. Did best change? Did goal?
That line ran, but the value stayed the same. Running a line doesn't always change a box.
Paused. Press Step to run one line at a time.
Welcome to the lab. Turn one dial with its minus and plus buttons, then press Run. Autopilot plays the same sky, so you can see what your change does.
Start lives at 1: press the minus on lives until it says 1, then press Run. How long does the game last now?
Make a star worth 5: press the plus on the star line until it says 5, then press Run. What happens to score? Why does the game end so soon?
Make a rock take 0: press the minus on the rock line until it says 0, then press Run. Which box stops changing?
Start speed at 5: press the plus on speed until it says 5, then press Run. Does the speed box ever change? Look at the if line.
Start score at 10: press the plus on score until it says 10, then press Run. Did Autopilot catch more stars, or did score just start higher?
Make a rock take 2: press the plus on the rock line until it says 2, then press Run. Look at lives at the end. Can a variable go below zero?
Press Run again without changing anything. Which boxes start over, and which keep their value?
Saved to your notebook.
Look at lives. The program took away more than was left, so it went below zero.
Here are your runs. Drag each card into a bin, or press Same or Changed on it. Then press Check with my runs.
No runs yet. Go to the Lab, press Run, then press Save to notebook.
Nice work. Your runs are the evidence.
Some cards say Look again. Move each one to the other bin, then press Check with my runs again.
Put every card in a bin, then press Check with my runs again.
Press Play to start. Move the ship with the arrow buttons or the arrow keys. Each box is a variable: watch which line changes it.
Turn one dial with its minus and plus buttons, then press Run. Autopilot plays the same sky every time, so only your number makes the difference.
Move the ship with the arrow buttons or the arrow keys. Press Pause to stop and look at the boxes.
Autopilot is flying. Watch the boxes change, or press Pause and then Step to run one line.
